voyage.name: Museum of Islamic Arts
voyage.address: Next to Doha Port, on the Corniche
voyage.content: Doha's flagship museum. Housed in a building designed by I.M. Pei, the museum hosts artefacts from Muslim dynasties all over Asia, Africa and Europe. Also present are items from the Al-Thani dynasty, as well as art from all parts of the Middle East. Gloriously air conditioned, there is also a cafe and gift shop. The permanent exhibition is on the 2nd and 3rd floors, with temporary exhibitions on the ground floor. Fre

voyage.name: Mathaf: Arab Museum of Modern Art
voyage.price: QR 50, or QR 85 for a museum pass
voyage.content: A specially designed building housing a collection of modern art from the Arab world, based on a personal collection amassed by Sheikh Hamad bin Khalifa Al Thani. The museum also hosts occasional exhibits featuring internationally-recognized contemporary artists. An hourly shuttle service provides free transportation between MIA and Mathaf W Th Sa Su 11:00-17:00, F 15:00-20:00, no shuttle M Tu; driving time between t

voyage.name: National Museum of Qatar
voyage.content: Opened in early 2019. The original museum was housed in an early 20th-century palace; its extension, now under construction, was designed by French architect Jean Nouvel and inspired by the desert sand rose. The extension and original palace can both still be viewed from the outside.

voyage.name: Orientalist Museum
voyage.content: The Orientalist Collection of the State of Qatar is one of the most significant collections ever assembled in the world. The approximate 700 paintings, water colours, drawings and prints trace Orientalism back to the early 18th century. The museum closes sporadically and it may be difficult to get an appointment.

voyage.name: Arab Postal Stamp Museum
voyage.content: Established in 2010, this small museum exhibits stamps from 22 Arab countries.

voyage.name: Sheikh Faisal bin Qassim Museum: West Bay Branch
voyage.address: City Tower, 6th Floor, Omar Al Mukhtar St
voyage.content: An extension of the Sheikh Faisal bin Qassim Museum in Al Shahaniyah, this branch displays carpets from various Middle Eastern countries, and furniture and domestic objects from Qatar and the Gulf region. It is eventually planned to make the collection accessible without appointment.

voyage.name: VCUQatar Gallery
voyage.address: Virginia Commonwealth University in Qatar, Al Luqta Street, Education City
voyage.content: VCUQatar have a small gallery, with exhibitions which change every few months, in their campus on Education City, which is open to everyone (sign in at reception). Because of the ongoing building works at Education City, it's a nightmare to get from Mathaf to here, but when the trams are running it should be an easy side-trip from there!

voyage.name: Msheireb Museums
voyage.hours: Mon-Sat 09:00-17:00; open Fri until 21:, closed Sun
voyage.content: A collection of four historic houses in the new downtown district of Msheireb: Mohammed bin Jassim House, Company House, Bin Jelmood House and Radwani House. They feature exhibits on the Msheireb community, traditional Qatari family life, the history of the oil industry, and slavery and exploitation.

voyage.name: Firestation Artist in Residence
voyage.content: Has an art supply store and cafe on site.

voyage.name: Al Koot Fort
voyage.content: Built in 1880 during the Ottoman period, this big white fort is in what is now the parking lot of Souq Waqif. At the time it was built, however, the fort was on the outskirts of the city. It was used as an ethnographic museum, the building is undergoing renovations and is closed, although it is still a popular place to take photos.

voyage.name: Fanar Qatar Islamic Cultural Center
voyage.content: Easily spotted from the Corniche with its distinctive spiral minaret, the center aims to educate non-Muslims about Islam by offering free Arabic classes as well as art and calligraphy exhibits. The center conducts bi-weekly tours of local mosques followed by a traditional dinner (abayas provided for women, registration required), and also hosts weekly coffee mornings with presentations on Qatari culture and lifestyle

voyage.name: Clock Tower
voyage.content: Next to the Grand Mosque, this old clock tower features Arabic numerals on its face. The tower is also on a hill, and as such offers some wonderful views of the Corniche.

voyage.name: Windtower House
voyage.address: Grand Hamad St & Ali bin Abdulla St
voyage.content: One of the last traditional windtowers in Qatar. Windtowers were used in the days before air conditioning, functioning by sucking cool air into a house. The house is not open to the public, but can be viewed from the outside.

voyage.name: Souq Waqif
voyage.content: Souq Waqif is the renovated Arabic market quarter, where one can easily wander around the maze-like corridors for hours. The souq is organized more or less by what is sold. There is a section of spice shops, another of textiles, and even a quarter with falcons for sale. Stables with Arabian horses are not far from the falcons, and camels are kept near Al Koot Fort and the parking lot. Also look for places to buy souv

voyage.name: Msheireb Enrichment Centre
voyage.address: barge docked off the Corniche, next to the Sheraton
voyage.content: A small museum with photographs and artifacts illustrating the historic development of Doha from small fishing town to modern city. The exhibit is sponsored by developer of the Msheireb project near Souq Waqif.

voyage.name: Heritage Library
voyage.content: Over 51,000 books in Arabic and other languages on Qatar and the Middle East, together with 600 antique maps, 2,000 manuscripts and 6,000 original photographs, form the Arabian and Islamic Heritage Library in Qatar, another initiative of HH Sheikha Mozah Bint Nasser Al Missned through Qatar Foundation. It is one of the largest research centres in the Middle East, and is based on a collection started by Sheikh Hassan

voyage.name: Qatar National Library
voyage.content: Opened in April 2018, the building was designed by renowned Dutch architect Rem Koolhaas.

voyage.name: Virginia Commonwealth University Gallery
voyage.content: The gallery at the VCU-Q campus in Education City regularly hosts visiting exhibitions and the work of faculty members and students. On those occasions, the gallery is open to the general public. The collection includes Arab manuscripts, a foreign language section dating back to the 15th century, and 20th century books about art and politics.

voyage.name: Heritage Village
voyage.content: Its buildings are modeled on a traditional Qatari village. Visitors can expect to see weaving, pearl trading, and a dhow (traditional boat). The village is open only for Ramadan, Eid, and special cultural festivals.

voyage.name: Al Najada
voyage.content: For a glimpse of some older Qatari architecture, it can be worthwhile to wander around some of the older neighborhoods surrounding Souq Waqif, particularly the small neighborhood to the immediate south of the souq. There are still a few notable old villas and mosques which predate the mostly 1970s-era buildings; given the pace of redevelopment in Doha it is unclear how much longer they will survive. Best explored on

voyage.name: House of Sheikh Abdullah bin Thani Al-Thani
voyage.content: A traditional Qatari home, remarkable because it has two instead of one 'majlis' (guest reception area). Built in 1935 using traditional materials and techniques, it has been fully restored. The building is not open to the public, but can be viewed from the outside.

voyage.name: Corniche
voyage.content: The visual highlight of Doha is Al-Corniche, a long seaside promenade that curves around Doha Bay and affords pretty views of Palm Tree Island and the city's skyscrapers. In the afternoons you will see plenty of locals strolling, often trying to get out of the way of the odd crazy Western ex-pat on rollerblades. It's also a good place for jogging. Cycling is prohibited. If you're looking to have the scenery all to yo

voyage.name: Al Bidda Park
voyage.content: Formerly known as Rumeila Park, this is opposite the Corniche with an outdoor theatre, art gallery, water features, children’s play area and skateboard/rollerblading half-pipe. There is a metro station, several shops, a third-wave coffee shop, and public toilets.

voyage.name: Katara Cultural Village
voyage.content: This building complex is designed to resemble a traditional Qatari village, and includes a large open-air amphitheater, opera house, drama theater, galleries, as well as a number of (expensive) restaurants featuring international cuisine. The galleries host changing art and photography exhibits, and various festivals are held here throughout the year. There is also a public beach here (entry fee QR 100) which offers

voyage.name: Al Jazeera Studios
voyage.content: One of Qatar's claims to fame is the Al Jazeera news network, which broadcasts to hundreds of millions around the world. The studios are not made to be a tourist attraction, although you may be able to contact the office and ask for a tour. A small on-site museum is dedicated to journalists who have died in the field, and has various timelines and displays about the network's history.

voyage.name: Doha Zoo
voyage.content: The zoo is undergoing major renovation and refurbishment, and is closed.

voyage.name: MIA Park
voyage.hours: Oct-May: Wed-Mon 10:30-23:30, Jun-Sep: Wed-Mon 18:00-00:00, closed 1 Jul - 2nd day of Eid
voyage.content: This modern park was built on reclaimed land and affords great views of the West Bay skyline. Visitors can rent bicycles or paddleboats, and enjoy coffee or ice cream at a small café. At the end of the promenade is the monumental sculpture '7' by American sculptor Richard Serra. During the winter the MIA Park Bazaar is held on the first Saturday of every month, offering an eclectic mix of food, arts, crafts, books, a

voyage.name: Calligraffiti Murals
voyage.address: four underground tunnels on Salwa Rd
voyage.content: In 2013 the French-Tunisian graffiti artist eL Seed was commissioned by the Qatar Museum Authority and the Public Works Authority to paint a series of 52 large-scale murals inspired by Qatari culture. The project required four months to complete and showcases eL Seed's signature style fusing Arabic calligraphy with street art. The murals can be best seen by simply driving through the tunnels.

voyage.name: The Miraculous Journey
voyage.content: A series of 14 monumental bronze sculptures depicting the stages of development of a fetus from gestation to newborn, by British artist Damien Hirst. The sculptures were commissioned by the Qatar Museum Authority, which reportedly paid US$20 million for them. The medical center is a women's hospital.

voyage.name: Ministry of Interior building
voyage.content: A massive and actually quite sinister building resembling a fort, (usually) only to be seen from outside during a drive around.

voyage.name: Asian Town
voyage.content: A mall, activity centre, amphitheatre, cricket stadium and accommodations catering to migrant workers. Cricket matches are a truly unique experience, and the mall boasts Qatar's cheapest prices. It is controversial for its alleged usage to isolate migrant workers from broader society (though defenders argue it provides much needed housing and community for migrant workers), and is unfortunately often considered a no-

voyage.name: Beaches
voyage.content: There are well-maintained private beaches in Doha owned by hotels, which permit public access for a fee. Hotels with beaches include the Grand Hyatt, Diplomatic Club, InterContinental, Sheraton, Sharq Village, and the Four Seasons, with fees ranging from QR 180 for weekday passes to annual family memberships. Additionally, the Katara Cultural Village operates Doha's only public beach, with an entry fee of QR 100. On

voyage.name: Dhow tour
voyage.content: Day or evening dhow cruises can be arranged with any of the dhows docked along the Corniche. Many cruises offer meals and entertainment, and can be booked for large tours or for more informal arrangements.

voyage.name: Doha Film Institute
voyage.content: Showcasing a wide range of international and art films, DFI also hosts two international film festivals, in November and in March. Films are screened at the Museum of Islamic Art and at Katara Cultural Village; tickets can be booked online.

voyage.name: Doha Golf Club
voyage.content: The only golf club open to the general public.

voyage.name: Drag racing
voyage.content: Drag racing is promoted by the Qatari government on an organized racetrack so young drivers do not feel the need for crazy driving on the streets of Doha. For a fee you can race your own car, or you can watch one of the regularly-scheduled professional races.

voyage.name: Jungle Zone
voyage.content: 3500 m² of animal-themed children's attractions, Qatar's most popular indoor theme park.

voyage.name: Kayaking
voyage.content: Entalek Adventures offers guided sea kayaking trips within Doha, or further afield along coastal mangroves and secluded beaches, with opportunities for birdwatching and camping. They also conduct guided snorkeling trips, and can rent out fully-outfitted kayaks (QR 200/day).

voyage.name: Qatar Racing and Equestrian Club
voyage.content: Horse racing takes place during the winter months, with races scheduled every Thursday beginning at 16:00 and lasting until about 21:00 Gambling is prohibited, but attendees can enter free raffles to guess the winning horses, with substantial prizes (including cars). These races are very popular. The showpiece race here is the HH The Amir Sword, held in February every year, one of the most prestigious races in the wo

voyage.name: Sailing
voyage.content: Regatta Sailing Academy offers sailing courses and a range of boats for hire, including funboats, dinghies, and two 30-foot yachts.

voyage.name: Sheesha
voyage.content: A typical Middle Eastern activity in the afternoons is to find a sheesha cafe and smoke some fruit-flavoured tobacco. One of the best places in Doha is Ras-Naswa at the non-Sheraton end of the Corniche. It's in a picturesque old-style building reminiscent, in colour and texture if not grandeur, of the red Mughal structures in India. Ras-Naswa has a nice outdoor garden and serves decent Middle Eastern food.

voyage.name: Al Shaqab Horse Centre
voyage.content: A state of the art horse riding facility and equestrian centre highlighting the importance of the Arabian horse and the detailing the history of equestrianism in the area.

voyage.name: Aspire Park
voyage.content: The largest park in Doha. Lots of grass, trees, playgrounds.

voyage.name: Souq Waqif
voyage.content: Also referred to as the Old Souq, this is the best place to pick up souvenirs and rub shoulder with locals. There are good restaurants and sheesha cafes here. There are also falcon shops, and some dealers will allow you to handle and photograph them. Also worth visiting are the horse stables (near the falcon shops) and the camels (near Al Koot Fort).

voyage.name: Gold Souq
voyage.content: The place to buy gold and jewellery. The purity of gold is strictly regulated, so you can be sure of the quality.

voyage.name: Fabric Souq
voyage.content: This comprises three different neighboring souqs (Al Ahmed, Al Asiery, and Al Dira). Here you can choose from a selection of exotic fabrics and have clothing designed and tailored to your specifications. For a complete outfit, allow about a week or two for completion.

voyage.name: Omani Souq
voyage.content: Here you can buy things like spices, incense and woven baskets. Next door is a vegetable market.

voyage.name: City Center Doha
voyage.content: The largest shopping centre in Qatar. In West Bay, the modern part of the city on the northern end of the Corniche, it offers a large and diverse shopping experience, including several jewellery and perfume stores. For entertainment there is a large multiplex cinema, a bowling alley, a children's arcade, as well as an indoor ice skating rink. There are several eating options including two food courts and several sit-

voyage.name: Ezdan Mall
voyage.content: One of Doha's greatest malls, with 200 tenants and a Carrefour supermarket. Not all shops are open yet.

voyage.name: The Gate Shopping Center
voyage.content: 280 shops with mostly luxury goods. The popular bistro 'Jones the Grocer' is also here.

voyage.name: Hyatt Plaza
voyage.content: This shopping mall is smaller than others, but as a plus it is always less crowded. There is a good sized food court and a large children's playland called "Jungle Zone."

voyage.name: Lagoona Plaza
voyage.content: Mostly high-end luxury goods, with a Carrefour grocery store.

voyage.name: Landmark Shopping Mall
voyage.content: Focuses mostly on clothing, jewellery, and cosmetics. There is also a Carrefour hypermarket for groceries.

voyage.name: The Mall
voyage.address: Najma St and D Ring Rd
voyage.content: Tourists are better off going to any of the aforementioned locations if they wish to purchase store goods.

voyage.name: Villaggio Shopping Mall
voyage.content: Near the Aspire Centre. The mall is designed to look like Venice in terms of architecture, and is home to many western stores, as well as a large Carrefour. The food court is home to several Western-style fast food restaurants, and several sit-down options. For entertainment, there is a long canal offering gondola rides (QR 15), an ice-skating rink (QR 30), and a cinema with 13 screens and one IMAX screen.

voyage.name: Mall of Qatar
voyage.content: One of the newer malls, located on the outskirts of Al Rayyan, with numerous luxury brands.

voyage.name: Place Vendôme
voyage.content: Located in the new development area of Lusail just north of Doha, this luxury shopping mall is extraordinarily opulent and designed based on the traditional French architectural style.

voyage.name: Jarir Bookstore (Salwa)
voyage.content: Sells Arabic and English language books, and a good selection of international magazines and newspapers. Also has a Costa coffee bar. There is a second branch near Education City, on Al Rayyan Al Jadeed Rd.

voyage.name: Virgin Megastore
voyage.content: Stocks books and magazines in Arabic, English, and French. A second branch in Landmark Mall has a much smaller selection.

voyage.name: Ric's Kountry Kitchen
voyage.address: Sana Complex, Ras Abu Abboud St
voyage.content: Serves up large classic American breakfasts, and one of the few places in Doha with real bacon and pork sausages.

voyage.name: Yellow Cab Pizza
voyage.content: This is undisputedly the most popular pizza in Doha, surprisingly offered by a well-established and efficient Filipino operation. The barbequed chicken pizza is particularly tasty. Delivery and pick-up available.

voyage.name: Noodle House
voyage.phone: +974 4411 5063 (City Center Mall), +974 4417 5682 (Landmark Mall), +974 4495 3876 (The Pearl-Qatar Porto Arabia)
voyage.content: Offers a number of southeast Asian-style dishes. Their portions are not very large, but the taste makes up for that. Their prawn crackers are particularly good. Delivery available.

voyage.name: Oishi Sushi
voyage.content: Decent sushi, with sushi train. On Monday and Tuesday evenings they offer an all-you-can-eat for QR 135 (reservations recommended).

voyage.name: Royal Bafilyon
voyage.content: This Cantonese restaurant is a favorite of the Chinese and Singaporean expat communities.

voyage.name: Shanghai Garden
voyage.content: Favoured by local Chinese expats.

voyage.name: Thai Corner
voyage.content: Tiny place with two tables, with fantastic Thai food. In nice weather you can eat in the courtyard.

voyage.name: Thai Smile
voyage.content: Casual and delicious Thai street food, with outdoor seating.

voyage.name: Thai Snack
voyage.content: A Doha institution, offers authentic Thai street food for very reasonable prices.

voyage.name: Yee Hwa Restaurant
voyage.content: This restaurant specialises in Korean barbecue and Japanese cuisine, and is one of the better places in Doha for sushi.

voyage.name: Ciao
voyage.content: Offers thin-crust pizza baked in a traditional oven, along with a good selection of pastas and risottos.

voyage.name: J&G Sandwich Cellar
voyage.content: Doha's only British café, with full English breakfasts and Yorkshire pudding. Free Wi-Fi; delivery and takeout available.

voyage.name: Lo Spaghetto
voyage.address: corner of Al Difaaf and Al Hamdani St
voyage.content: Classic Italian food, prepared by Italian chefs.

voyage.name: Mykonos
voyage.content: Solid Greek food, outdoor pool-side seating available.

voyage.name: Aalishan
voyage.content: Recommended for the Friday afternoon buffet.

voyage.name: Al Zarka
voyage.content: Very popular with South Asian workers as well as Qataris. Menu features primarily Indian as well as Arabian dishes.

voyage.name: Anjappar Chettinad
voyage.content: Vegetarian, good value for the thali set menu.

voyage.name: Bukhara
voyage.content: Delicious northern Indian cuisine, with especially good fish tandoori and chicken vindaloo.

voyage.name: Chingari
voyage.content: Expensive and good northern Indian food, with live Indian music on a small stage.

voyage.name: Garden Annapoorna
voyage.content: It serves great south Indian dishes.

voyage.name: The Garden Village Restaurant Doha
voyage.content: Recommended for its good ambience and nice Indian village model interior.

voyage.name: Spice and Sizzles
voyage.address: Salwa Road, Building 158 , Street No 340 , Zone 55
voyage.content: A luxurious Pakistani/Indian/Asian restaurant.

voyage.name: Al Shami Home Restaurant
voyage.content: A Doha institution, featuring traditional Syrian and Lebanese dishes, and sheesha.

voyage.name: Al Hamra
voyage.content: A family restaurant offering Lebanese dishes. Service is a bit slow, good for large groups.

voyage.name: Al Mourjan
voyage.content: An upscale place with tasty Lebanese dishes and some of the best views in Doha.

voyage.name: Ankara Pastry Restaurant
voyage.content: Good pastries and shwarmas, popular with Turkish expats.

voyage.name: Istanbul Sultan
voyage.content: Very small place with great schwarmas.

voyage.name: Layali
voyage.content: One of the more expensive Lebanese restaurants. It is rumored that the former Emir has eaten here on occasion.

voyage.name: Shebestan Palace Restaurant
voyage.content: Good Persian food.

voyage.name: Turkey Central
voyage.content: Offers good, cheap Middle Eastern fare. The portions are large (try the mixed grill or shish tawooq) and the appetizers are excellent, particularly the chili labneh. Delivery and take-out available.

voyage.name: Shay Al Shoomos
voyage.content: A popular breakfast spot, and one of the few very few places that serves traditional Qatari cuisine.

voyage.name: Parisa
voyage.content: Excellent Persian cuisine in unique surroundings. Booking advised.

voyage.name: Best Fish
voyage.content: Popular with Qataris. Cheap local fish dishes: the grilled hammour with garlic butter is recommended. Take away and home delivery available.

voyage.name: Fish Market
voyage.content: The best fish in town at upscale prices, much of it local. Reservations recommended, particularly for the Friday brunch.

voyage.name: L'wzaar Seafood Market
voyage.content: A good selection of seafood, with good views. Reservations recommended.

voyage.name: Carrefour
voyage.content: This French chain has three hypermarkets in Doha: in Landmark Mall, Villaggio Mall, and City Center Mall. They also have a smaller grocery store in Lagoona Plaza.

voyage.name: Family Food Centre
voyage.hours: 7:30AM-midnight daily, closed Fri for midday prayer
voyage.content: Three branches on Al Matar St, Al Mirqab Al Jadeed St, and Al Rayyan.

voyage.name: LuLu
voyage.hours: Daily 08:00-00:00, closed Fri for midday prayer
voyage.content: This UAE-based chain operates two full hypermarkets: on D-Ring Rd (near the airport) and in Al Gharrafa (across from Landmark Mall). There is also a smaller express store near Education City, and a branch has been opened in Al Messila.

voyage.name: Mega Mart
voyage.content: Very popular with western expats as it imports a lot of products from America and Europe, but can be quite expensive. Also has a Costa Coffee nearby, as well as many smaller shops stocking cards, electronics and perfumes.

voyage.name: PappaRoti
voyage.content: This branch of the popular Malaysian café chain offers a good selection of coffee and teas, along with special roti buns.

voyage.name: Doha B - Qatar Youth Hostels Association
Abraj Suites Hotel
voyage.address: Building 6, Street 867, Hisham Bin Oqba St, Al Mansoura
voyage.content: All-suite hotel opened in 2025 with 161 one-bedroom suites of 55–65 m², each with a separate living room, a full kitchen with washing machine and two bathrooms. Rooftop pool, gym, spa, a restaurant and free basement parking. Rents by the night, month or year. No alcohol.

voyage.name: Al Madina Suites
voyage.price: Rates on official website start at QR 450
voyage.content: The hotel offers well-furnished suites all equipped with air-conditioner, Internet connection, cable TV, and coffee/tea maker. Some of its facilities are fitness room/gym, airport and city transfers, tours and excursion desk, and laundry service.

voyage.name: Al Muntazah Plaza Hotel
voyage.content: Fully furnished 2- to 3- bedroom apartments and standard hotel rooms, on the prestigious Al-Muntazah Road convenient for the corniche, city centre, airport, supermarkets and the shopping centres.

voyage.name: Hotel Crystal Palace
voyage.price: Rates on official website start at QR 239
voyage.address: corner of Al Fairouz St and Al Fayaa St
voyage.content: The hotel offers cozy rooms, all of which have air-conditioner, cable TV, mini-bar, and safe. Some of its amenities are Wi-Fi connectivity, health club, business centre, and laundry service.

voyage.name: Doha Marriott Hotel
voyage.content: In a slightly out of the way location, but since nowhere in Doha is really walkable, that's not a huge strike against it. It has two towers of excellent 4-star rooms and a selection of restaurants few hotels can match: the Mexican is acceptable, the pan-Asian quite good, the buffet nothing special, and the Indian really great. Alcohol is available in the restaurants, but there is no cocktail lounge or bar. There is a

voyage.name: Mercure Doha
voyage.content: A 4-star hotel belonging to the Accor group pretty much in the town centre. It has a sauna, a swimming pool and various restaurants. Shuttle buses go regularly from and to the airport. You can walk around and see things just outside the door (unlike most Doha hotels, which are someone isolated), but it is also a little less tranquil.

voyage.name: Mövenpick Hotel Doha
voyage.content: 4-star hotel on the Corniche with an all day dining restaurant and piano bar.

voyage.name: Ramada Encore Doha
voyage.address: Ahmed Bin Mohammed Bin Thani St
voyage.content: A comfortable 4-star hotel with a few pleasant surprises. The Indian restaurant is one of the best in town (and, because it's in a hotel, it serves alcohol). The pub on the hotel's ground floor is a large club that on weekends comes alive as a disco under the guidance of a Filipino cover band and hundreds of Asian workers letting loose after a hard 6-day work week. The Library Bar, on the hotel's top floor, has a sma

voyage.name: Somerset West Bay Doha
voyage.content: The property offers 2- and 3-bedroom apartments. Facilities include a gymnasium, recreation room, indoor swimming pool and children’s playroom.

voyage.name: Banana Island Resort Doha by Anantara
voyage.content: On the shores of Doha on the Arabian Gulf.

voyage.name: Four Seasons
voyage.content: The first five-star hotel in town. It has a great but expensive Italian restaurant and a decent cigar/cocktail lounge just off the lobby. The pool and beach area are for hotel guests and spa members only.

voyage.name: Grand Hyatt Doha
voyage.content: Most of the suites & rooms have breathtaking views of the Persian Gulf and feature balconies or terraces.

voyage.name: Imperial Suites Hotels Doha
voyage.content: 5 minutes away from the airport. Rooms are equipped with rich fabric bed, LCD TV with DVD player and fully equipped kitchen. Some of its facilities and services are Omssiyat restaurant, fitness room/ gym, 24-hour room service and airport transfer.

voyage.name: InterContinental Doha
voyage.content: Five minutes up the coast from the town centre and directly across the road from the seemingly never open Alladin's Kingdom amusement park. The pool and beach complex at are large, quiet and relaxing. The restaurants are nothing special, but the rooms are great and the nightlife decent.

voyage.name: InterContinental Doha - The City
voyage.address: Off Al Wahda Rd, City Center

voyage.name: La Cigale Hotel
voyage.content: A member of The Leading Hotels of the World, in the heart of the city and only 15 minutes by car from the airport. 225 luxurious rooms and suites; 11 dining and entertainment outlets offering a selection of cuisine including Italian, Japanese, Mediterranean, Middle Eastern and Oriental and evening chill-out options; two ballrooms; a well-equipped gymnasium with certified instructors; an indoor swimming pool and a del

voyage.name: Merwebhotel Central Doha
voyage.content: 5-star hotel designed to meet the needs of business travellers through the use of innovative technologies and tailor made services adding a subtle flair of Qatari hospitality and heritage.

voyage.name: Mövenpick Tower & Suites
voyage.content: 26-storey tower at the entrance to West Bay, 15 minutes drive from the airport. 350 rooms and suites. Facilities include conference rooms and restaurants.

voyage.name: The Ritz-Carlton
voyage.content: 10-minute drive north of the heart of Doha, along the Gulf Coast. It has great service and luxury rooms, all for the price you'd expect to pay at a Ritz-Carlton. The pool complex is large and landscaped to look an oasis, complete with fake rocks and waterfall. There's also a swim-up bar in the pool. The cigar bar/cocktail lounge is small, but the balcony has great views of the marina and pool. Friday brunch at the Ri

voyage.name: Sheraton Grand Doha
voyage.content: The Sheraton is an architectural and minor cultural landmark in Doha, having been in town longer than any other international hotel. Shaped like a pyramid with an Imperial Star Destroyer stuck on top, it is at one end of the Corniche, making it visible from that long, waterfront road and walkway.

voyage.name: The Torch Doha
voyage.content: In the distinctive 300-m-high Aspire Tower built for the Asian Games, the Torch Hotel offers modern-appointed rooms over 51 floors. There is also a rotating restaurant which offers 360° panoramic views of the city.

voyage.name: W Doha Hotel
voyage.content: Urban sanctuary that provides luxury accommodation and lifestyle.

voyage.name: Singing Sand Dunes
voyage.content: In the desert 40 km southwest of Doha are the so-called Singing Sand Dunes. This is one of 30 sites in the world with "singing" sand, once attributed to evil djinn. When the humidity is low and the wind blows along the sand, an eerie humming sound can be heard, which can be amplified by running across the sand, or by sledding down it. Large plastic bags (e.g. garbage bags) or large pieces of cardboard work particular

voyage.name: Dhal Al Misfir
voyage.content: The most well-known of Qatar's caves, this 40 m-deep formation contains fibrous, faintly phosphorescent gypsum crystals. There is also a resident flock of cave-dwelling Little Owls (Athene noctua). For safety reasons the site is surrounded by a chainlink fence but the gate is unlocked and visitors may enter freely.

voyage.name: Mudhlem Cave
voyage.content: A 150 m-deep cave not far from the Misfir Sinkhole. The mouth is about 15m wide and there is a pool of brackish water at the bottom, which was once used as a source of drinking water by the local Bedouin. The cave is now a popular geocache site.

voyage.name: Doha Sub Aqua Club
voyage.content: A branch of the British Sub Aqua Club, offers a range of diving courses based on BSAC qualifications. Also arranges shore dives and offshore wreck dives weekly.

voyage.name: Q-Dive Marine Center
voyage.content: Offers a full range of diving services, including equipment sales and rental and PADI dive courses. Arranges diving, snorkeling and fishing trips.

voyage.name: Qatar Divers
voyage.content: Offers a full range of PADI courses, and organizes dives around Qatar.
